programs.name: regrid3
programs.purpose: Resample a three-dimensional binary float grid onto a grid of different dimensions.
programs.selfdoc_first_line: REGRID3 - REwrite a [ni3][ni2][ni1] GRID to a [no3][no2][no1] 3-D grid

params.name: ni1
params.description: Fast input dimension.

params.name: ni2
params.description: Middle input dimension.

params.name: ni3
params.description: Slow input dimension.

params.name: no1
params.description: Fast output dimension.

params.name: no2
params.description: Middle output dimension.

params.name: no3
params.description: Slow output dimension.

params.name: verbose
params.description: Print grid dimensions when nonzero.

programs.float_sensitive_notes: Interpolation uses float coordinates and a fixed nested expression. The source applies alpha1 to the third-axis branch and alpha3 to the first-axis branch; preserve this ordering. The validation allows no1=0 despite its positive-dimension error message.
programs.difficulty_reason: It buffers and interpolates an entire three-dimensional grid.

test_cases.description: Expand a two-dimensional grid into three dimensions.
test_cases.command: suplane nt=8 ntr=4 | sustrip head=/dev/null | regrid3 ni1=8 ni2=4 ni3=1 no1=6 no2=3 no3=2 verbose=1 > out.bin

test_cases.description: Resample all three axes of a small grid.
test_cases.command: suplane nt=8 ntr=8 | sustrip head=/dev/null | regrid3 ni1=8 ni2=4 ni3=2 no1=5 no2=3 no3=3 > out.bin

programs.name: resamp
programs.purpose: Resample the fast dimension of a binary float array using sinc interpolation.
programs.selfdoc_first_line: RESAMP - RESAMPle the 1st dimension of a 2-dimensional function f(x1,x2)

params.name: n1
params.default: computed: input file size in bytes divided by sizeof(float)
params.description: Input samples per row; omission requires seekable input.

params.name: n2
params.description: Number of rows; a negative value reads until a complete row cannot be read.

params.name: d1
params.description: Input sample interval.

params.name: f1
params.description: First input coordinate.

params.name: n1r
params.description: Output samples per row.

params.name: d1r
params.description: Output sample interval.

params.name: f1r
params.description: First output coordinate.

programs.float_sensitive_notes: Eight-point sinc interpolation uses library-generated coefficients and floating-point arithmetic. Output coordinates are generated by repeated float addition; there is no anti-alias filter.
programs.difficulty_reason: It uses eight-point sinc interpolation on each input row.

test_cases.description: Resample multiple rows with a shifted output origin.
test_cases.command: suplane nt=32 ntr=4 | sustrip head=/dev/null | resamp n1=32 n2=4 d1=0.004 f1=0 n1r=20 d1r=0.006 f1r=0.002 > out.bin

test_cases.description: Infer the input row length from a seekable file.
test_cases.command: suplane nt=32 ntr=1 | sustrip head=/dev/null > in.bin && resamp n1r=16 d1r=2 < in.bin > out.bin

programs.name: subset
programs.purpose: Select samples from a three-dimensional binary float array.
programs.selfdoc_first_line: SUBSET - select a SUBSET of the samples from a 3-dimensional file

params.name: n1
params.default: computed: input file size in bytes divided by sizeof(float)
params.description: Fast input dimension; omission requires seekable input.

params.name: n2
params.default: computed: input file size in bytes divided by n1*sizeof(float)
params.description: Middle input dimension; omission requires seekable input.

params.name: n3
params.default: computed: input file size in bytes divided by n2*n1*sizeof(float)
params.description: Slow input dimension; omission requires seekable input.

params.name: id1s
params.description: Fast-axis index increment, used when ix1s is absent.

params.name: if1s
params.description: First fast-axis index, used when ix1s is absent.

params.name: n1s
params.description: Number of fast-axis indices, used when ix1s is absent.

params.name: ix1s
params.description: Explicit fast-axis indices; overrides the other fast-axis selection parameters.

params.name: id2s
params.description: Middle-axis index increment, used when ix2s is absent.

params.name: if2s
params.description: First middle-axis index, used when ix2s is absent.

params.name: n2s
params.description: Number of middle-axis indices, used when ix2s is absent.

params.name: ix2s
params.description: Explicit middle-axis indices; overrides the other middle-axis selection parameters.

params.name: id3s
params.description: Slow-axis index increment, used when ix3s is absent.

params.name: if3s
params.description: First slow-axis index, used when ix3s is absent.

params.name: n3s
params.description: Number of slow-axis indices, used when ix3s is absent.

params.name: ix3s
params.description: Explicit slow-axis indices; overrides the other slow-axis selection parameters.

programs.float_sensitive_notes: Samples are copied without arithmetic. Input must be seekable even when all dimensions are supplied; zero index increments can cause division by zero when the corresponding selection count is omitted.
programs.difficulty_reason: It supports arbitrary index arrays and seeks through a three-dimensional input file.

test_cases.description: Select regular strides along all axes.
test_cases.command: suplane nt=16 ntr=8 | sustrip head=/dev/null > in.bin && subset n1=16 n2=4 n3=2 id1s=2 if1s=1 id2s=2 if3s=1 < in.bin > out.bin

test_cases.description: Select explicit indices in reverse and repeated order.
test_cases.command: suplane nt=16 ntr=8 | sustrip head=/dev/null > in.bin && subset n1=16 n2=4 n3=2 ix1s=15,0,3 ix2s=3,1 ix3s=1,0 < in.bin > out.bin

programs.name: transp
programs.purpose: Transpose a two-dimensional matrix of fixed-size elements.
programs.selfdoc_first_line: TRANSP - TRANSPose an n1 by n2 element matrix

params.name: n1
params.description: Number of elements in the fast input dimension.

params.name: n2
params.default: computed: input file size in bytes divided by n1*nbpe
params.description: Number of elements in the slow input dimension; omission requires seekable input.

params.name: nbpe
params.description: Bytes per matrix element.

params.name: verbose
params.description: Print progress when nonzero.

programs.float_sensitive_notes: Elements are copied as bytes without floating-point arithmetic.
programs.difficulty_reason: It transposes a buffered matrix using the big-matrix library.

test_cases.description: Transpose a matrix from a pipe with explicit dimensions.
test_cases.command: suplane nt=16 ntr=4 | sustrip head=/dev/null | transp n1=16 n2=4 nbpe=4 verbose=1 > out.bin

test_cases.description: Infer the second dimension from a file.
test_cases.command: suplane nt=16 ntr=4 | sustrip head=/dev/null > in.bin && transp n1=16 < in.bin > out.bin

programs.name: transp3d
programs.purpose: Permute the axes of a three-dimensional matrix of fixed-size elements.
programs.selfdoc_first_line: TRANSP3D - TRANSPose an n1 by n2 by n3 element matrix

params.name: n1
params.description: Fast input dimension.

params.name: n2
params.description: Middle input dimension.

params.name: n3
params.default: computed: input file size in bytes divided by n1*n2*nbpe
params.description: Slow input dimension; omission requires seekable input.

params.name: perm
params.description: Output axis order: 123, 132, 213, 231, 312, or 321.

params.name: nbpe
params.description: Bytes per matrix element.

params.name: scratchdir
params.description: Comma-separated directories for VND scratch files.

params.name: scratchstem
params.description: Scratch file name prefix.

params.name: verbose
params.description: Print progress when nonzero.

programs.float_sensitive_notes: Elements are copied as bytes without floating-point arithmetic. The default scratch-directory allocation uses ealloc2 and then copies /tmp into tempdirs[0]; reproduce its intended behavior rather than assuming its pointer layout is portable.
programs.difficulty_reason: It implements six axis permutations through a scratch-backed multidimensional array.

test_cases.description: Permute all three dimensions using the default ordering.
test_cases.command: suplane nt=8 ntr=8 | sustrip head=/dev/null | transp3d n1=8 n2=4 n3=2 perm=231 nbpe=4 scratchdir=/tmp scratchstem=oxwave231 verbose=1 > out.bin

test_cases.description: Exercise the third-axis read path and infer n3.
test_cases.command: suplane nt=8 ntr=8 | sustrip head=/dev/null > in.bin && transp3d n1=8 n2=4 perm=321 scratchdir=/tmp scratchstem=oxwave321 < in.bin > out.bin
suplane nt=8 ntr=8 | sustrip head=/dev/null | transp3d n1=8 n2=4 n3=2 perm=123 scratchdir=/tmp scratchstem=oxwave123 > out.bin

programs.name: unisam
programs.purpose: Interpolate input x,y pairs onto a uniform x grid, with optional sine additions and smoothing.
programs.selfdoc_first_line: UNISAM - UNIformly SAMple a function y(x) specified as x,y pairs

params.name: xin
params.description: Input x coordinates; required when no input files are named.

params.name: yin
params.description: Input y values; must match xin in length when using parameter arrays.

params.name: xfile
params.description: Binary file of x coordinates, used together with yfile.

params.name: yfile
params.description: Binary file of y values, used together with xfile.

params.name: xyfile
params.description: Binary file of interleaved x,y pairs; xfile and yfile take precedence when both are supplied.

params.name: npairs
params.description: Number of input pairs; required when reading xfile and yfile or xyfile.

params.name: nout
params.description: Number of output values.

params.name: dxout
params.description: Output coordinate interval.

params.name: fxout
params.description: First output coordinate.

params.name: method
params.description: Interpolation method, selected by first character: linear, mono, akima, or spline.

params.name: isint
params.description: Input interval indices for sine additions; an absent array means none.

params.name: amp
params.description: Sine amplitudes; required when 0 < count(isint) < nin-1.

params.name: phase0
params.description: Starting phases for sine additions.

params.name: totalphase
params.description: Total phases; supplied zero values are also replaced with PI.

params.name: nwidth
params.description: Window smoothing width; converted to nwidth/2*2+1 using integer arithmetic.

params.name: sloth
params.description: Interpolate values directly, reciprocals for 1, or reciprocal squares for 2, then convert output back.

params.name: smooth
params.description: Apply damped least-squares smoothing when nonzero.

params.name: r
params.description: Damping coefficient used by smooth_1.

programs.float_sensitive_notes: Interpolation methods and damped smoothing depend on floating-point operation order; sine additions call double-precision sin and sloth conversion calls sqrt. Window smoothing accumulates in float. Sine arrays are not initialized when count(isint) is at least nin-1, yet the later loop still accesses them; supplied sine arrays are not checked for matching lengths, and interval-derived output indices are not bounds-checked.
programs.difficulty_reason: It combines several interpolation methods, optional sine additions, and two smoothing paths.

test_cases.description: Interpolate explicit pairs with linear interpolation.
test_cases.command: unisam xin=0,1,2,3 yin=2,4,3,5 nout=7 dxout=0.5 fxout=0 method=linear > out.bin

test_cases.description: Use cubic interpolation, sine addition, and window smoothing.
test_cases.command: unisam xin=0,2,4,6 yin=2,3,5,4 nout=13 dxout=0.5 fxout=0 method=akima isint=1 amp=0.2 phase0=0.1 totalphase=3 nwidth=2 > out.bin

test_cases.description: Read separate generated binary files and apply sloth and damped smoothing.
test_cases.command: unisam xin=0,1 yin=0,3 nout=4 dxout=1 > x.bin && unisam xin=0,1 yin=2,5 nout=4 dxout=1 > y.bin && unisam xfile=x.bin yfile=y.bin npairs=4 nout=7 dxout=0.5 method=mono sloth=2 smooth=1 r=5 > out.bin

test_cases.description: Read interleaved pairs and use spline interpolation.
test_cases.command: unisam xin=0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7 yin=0,2,1,3,2,4,3,5 nout=8 dxout=1 > xy.bin && unisam xyfile=xy.bin npairs=4 nout=7 dxout=0.5 method=spline > out.bin
